Raw IMC Data QC: Pixel Intensity Distributions

Tazein Shah

2026-05-26

Overview

This notebook visualizes pixel-level ion count distributions from raw IMC TXT files — before any steinbock preprocessing. Each TXT file is one ROI; rows are pixels, columns are already labeled with both protein name and metal tag (e.g. SMA(Pr141Di)), so no external panel file is needed.

1. Load Libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(ggridges)

2. Read All TXT Files and Combine

TXT files live in the raw data directory, one per ROI. Column names already contain the protein name and metal tag (e.g. SMA(Pr141Di)), so no renaming is needed. We drop acquisition metadata and non-biological channels, apply arcsinh transformation (cofactor = 1), and stack everything into a single long-format tibble.

cofactor <- 1

txt_files <- list.files(
  path       = "/restricted/projectnb/camplab/projects/20220504_Suzuki_LN/Data/Imaging/IMC/Tumor/PardeeTumorAblations/Patient_14T/",
  pattern    = "\\.txt$",
  recursive  = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

# acquisition metadata and non-biological channels to drop
exclude_cols <- c("Start_push", "End_push", "Pushes_duration",
                  "X", "Y", "Z",
                  "DNA191(Ir191Di)", "DNA193(Ir193Di)", "Membrane(Pt196Di)")

raw_pixels <- map_dfr(txt_files, function(f) {
  df <- read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)

  df <- df %>% slice_sample(n = 50000)   # <-- add this

  df <- df %>% select(-any_of(exclude_cols))
  df <- df %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~asinh(. / cofactor)))

  fname      <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  df$roi     <- fname
  df$patient <- str_extract(fname, "^[^_]+")
  df
})

cat("Total pixels loaded:", nrow(raw_pixels), "\n")
## Total pixels loaded: 200000
cat("Patients found:", n_distinct(raw_pixels$patient), "\n")
## Patients found: 1
cat("ROIs found:", n_distinct(raw_pixels$roi), "\n")
## ROIs found: 4

3. Pivot to Long Format

plot_long <- raw_pixels %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -c(roi, patient),
    names_to  = "marker",
    values_to = "intensity"
  )

single_roi <- unique(plot_long$roi)[1]

---

## 4. Histograms: All Channels, One ROI

A quick per-channel histogram faceted view for a single ROI to get an overview
of the intensity landscape.


``` r
p <- plot_long %>%
  filter(roi == single_roi) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = intensity)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Pixel intensity distributions (arcsinh) — ", single_roi),
    subtitle = "Each panel = one protein marker; x-axis = arcsinh(count / 1)",
    x        = "arcsinh intensity",
    y        = "Pixel count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

p

ggsave("images/01_histogram_single_roi.png", plot = p, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 150)

5. Density Plots: Selected Markers Across All ROIs

Ridge plots let you compare intensity distributions across ROIs for a few markers of interest, which is useful for spotting between-ROI batch effects or acquisition issues.

p <- plot_long %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = intensity, y = roi, fill = patient)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.6, scale = 1.2, rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    title    = "Per-ROI pixel intensity distributions (all markers)",
    subtitle = "arcsinh(count / 1); each ridge = one ROI, color = patient",
    x        = "arcsinh intensity",
    y        = NULL,
    fill     = "Patient"
  ) +
  theme_ridges(font_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7))

p

ggsave("images/02_ridgeplot_all_markers.png", plot = p, width = 14, height = 40, dpi = 150)

6. Density Overlay: All Channels for One ROI

An alternative view: all markers overlaid in a single density plot to compare the signal spread across channels. Useful for spotting channels with no signal or unusually high background.

p <- plot_long %>%
  filter(roi == single_roi) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = intensity, color = marker)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("All-channel density overlay — ", single_roi),
    subtitle = "Channels with no biological signal will hug x = 0",
    x        = "arcsinh intensity",
    y        = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.text     = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"))

p

ggsave("images/03_density_overlay.png", plot = p, width = 14, height = 5, dpi = 150)

7. Summary Table: Per-Channel Median and % Zero Pixels

A numeric summary to flag channels with very low signal (high % zero pixels) or unexpected medians — useful for early QC before committing to preprocessing.

plot_long %>%
  group_by(marker) %>%
  summarise(
    median_intensity = round(median(intensity, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    pct_zero         = round(mean(intensity == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    max_intensity    = round(max(intensity, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_zero)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Per-channel pixel intensity summary (arcsinh-transformed)")
